# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1567
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1567
- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1567
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1567
- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1567._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-12):
**Red-gate drill (job 114778872699, head e68517b33) — fixed on f79482c7e.**

FILE:LINE (as reported):
- lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart:380:61, :384:16, :389:16 — `getter 'streamIdle'/'connect' isn't defined for the type 'Object?'`
- lib/src/providers/provider_tuning.dart:382:14, :387:17 — `argument type 'Duration?' can't be assigned to 'Duration'`

Root cause: `provider_tuning.dart` imports `provider_common.dart` through a `show` list that never included `ProviderTimeoutsOverride`. The new scoped-resolution helpers (`field`/`source`, issue #1554) named that type in their closure-parameter signatures — with the name unresolved the parameters collapsed to an invalid type, so every `.connect`/`.streamIdle` member read inside them errored (`Object?` getters) and the nullable global (`providerTimeoutsOverride`, type `ProviderTimeoutsOverride?`) flowed into the non-null typed pick (the `Duration?`→`Duration` pair). The old gh-1398 code never named the type (it leaned on the getter's inferred type), which is why the hole was invisible until this change.

Fix (one commit): add `ProviderTimeoutsOverride` to the show list + `if (global == null) return fallback;` guard before the typed pick. No behavior change.

Both-direction static proof per the PR#1557/#1565 lesson:
- (a) members → real declarations: `ProviderTimeoutsOverride.connect/streamIdle` grepped at provider_common.dart:863/866, getter at :877; `ProviderTuningEntry.connect/streamIdle/name`, `ResolvedProviderTimeouts` fields, `Model.connectTimeout/streamIdleTimeout/timeoutScopeLabel`, `ModelRef.connectTimeout/streamIdleTimeout/label`, `CustomModelDefinition`/`CustomProviderEntry` timeout fields, `createSseIterator(idleTimeout:, timeoutSource:)`, `sendProviderRequest/sendWatchedProviderRequest/_sendWatchedOnce` named params — each checked against its declaration.
- (b) type names written in new code → all resolve (core / in-file / now-imported / barrel-exported for tests).
- (c) over-80 scan on touched lines: clean — the 8 remaining >80 lines in provider_tuning.dart are byte-preexisting on main (section banners/doc lines); the one 81-char line I added was split, and the 90-char SKILL.md line reverted (mirrored into prompts.g.dart, sync count verified 0).
- dart VM remains SIGKILLed on this host (137) — this proof is static; CI is the compiler of record.

---

### Thread 2

**vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit** (2026-10-12):
**Red-gate drill, round 2 — both runs' FILE:LINEs, audit method, full finding list. Fixed on 3b7d27be1.**

## Findings (all fixed in one commit)

1. **Run 38248570659 — provider_tuning.dart:384:14 / :389:17** (`Duration?` → `Duration`): my `field()` helper was declared `Duration? field(...)` while its result feeds the non-null `ResolvedProviderTimeouts.connect/streamIdle`. The f79482c7e null-guard made every path return non-null but left the declared type nullable. **Fix:** return type `Duration` (null-guard → `fallback`; else `globalPick(global) ?? fallback`).
2. **Run 38248570659 — provider_common.dart:1217:60** (`getter 'scopeNote' isn't defined for '_IdleWatchdogSseIterator'`): a plain typo — the fire callback's local is `scopedNote`, the interpolation read ``, which resolves as an implicit `this.scopeNote` member read. **Not** a conditional-import twin gap: the fix is ``.
3. **Run 114778872699 (round 1) — provider_tuning.dart:380/382/384/387/389**: `ProviderTimeoutsOverride` missing from the `provider_common.dart` show list (fixed in f79482c7e, kept).

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

+## Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554)
+
+`connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive ints, ≤ 1 h) are
+valid on three config surfaces: `roles:` chain entries (map form),
+`customProviders:` entries, and `models.custom:` entries. Per FIELD, the
+first level that declares a value wins:
+
+```
+role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
+    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180 s, idle 300 s)
+```
+
+Per-field fallback: an entry overriding only `streamIdleTimeoutMs` leaves the
+connect leg at the lower levels. Configs without the keys behave
+byte-identically (the standing uncapped-run rule). When a scoped override is
+in effect the stall line names it (`idle window 1800s (role default
+override)`), so a wide window never reads as a hang.
+
+Slow-local-model recipe: a local endpoint that thinks minutes before the
+first byte needs the IDLE leg widened, not the whole config. On the role
+chain entry pinning the local endpoint set only `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2×`
+its worst silent prefill stretch — every cloud provider in the same config
+keeps the global watchdog untouched.
+

+roles:
+  default:
+    - provider: openai
+      model: local-thinker
+      baseUrl: http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1
+      streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # this entry only

- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

- **PR #**: 1567
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1567
- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1567
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1567
- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

{
  "key": "pr-1567",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals",
    "description": "Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

+## Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554)

+first byte needs the IDLE leg widened, not the whole config. On the role

+keeps the global watchdog untouched.

The new scoped-resolution helpers (`field`/`source`, issue #1554) named that type in their closure-parameter signatures — with the name unresolved the parameters collapsed to an invalid type, so every `.connect`/`.streamIdle` member read inside them errored (`Object?` getters) and the nullable global (`providerTimeoutsOverride`, type `ProviderTimeoutsOverride?`) flowed into the non-null typed pick (the `Duration?`→`Duration` pair). # SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

+## Scoped provider timeouts (issue #1554)

+`connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs` (strict positive ints, ≤ 1 h) are

+`customProviders:` entries, and `models.custom:` entries. Per FIELD, the
+first level that declares a value wins:

+role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
+    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180 s, idle 300 s)
+```

+connect leg at the lower levels. Configs without the keys behave
+byte-identically (the standing uncapped-run rule). When a scoped override is
+in effect the stall line names it (`idle window 1800s (role default
+override)`), so a wide window never reads as a hang.

+first byte needs the IDLE leg widened, not the whole config. On the role
+chain entry pinning the local endpoint set only `streamIdleTimeoutMs ≈ 2×`
+its worst silent prefill stretch — every cloud provider in the same config
+keeps the global watchdog untouched.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

The failing check is `kicker / sm-liveness` from the sm-kicker workflow — which is a watchdog/kicker job, not a test of the PR code. The known upstream defect awf#15 mentions crashes on zero-diff merge heads. The sm-liveness job is part of the factory watchdog. Without ci_failures_full.log, I can't see the exact error. Let me try fetching the run log via gh? Probably no network auth for that. Let me check if gh is available and try.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1567
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1567
- **Title**: feat(1554): scoped provider timeouts — roles chain entries + customProviders entries override the globals
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1554-scoped-provider-timeouts` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +638
- **Deletions**: -74
- **Created**: 2026-10-12T10:58:28Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

- Nothing known against the ACs. Non-goals respected: no auto-detection, no escalation-ladder changes, no per-model surface beyond `models:`.

## Verification / local-gate disclosure (honest)

- Targeted local gate attempted once per lane discipline: `dart test` on the three touched test files — **SIGKILLed (exit 137, machine guard), zero output** (the prompts regen script was killed the same way). **Static fallback** used instead: no new Dart files (all edits in existing files, directive order untouched); every referenced symbol verified defined/imported (barrel whole-file exports audited); ast-grep/tree-sitter parse of all 10 changed Dart files reported no parse issues; every changed call site audited (all pre-existing callers positional — additive named params only); 1:1 assertion trace against the implementation caught and fixed 2 wrong assertions in my own new tests before push. `prompts.g.dart` was hand-synced to `scripts/gen_prompts.dart`'s exact escaping (\`dartStringLiteral\`: `'`→`\'`, `$`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, non-ASCII raw) — `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` is the byte-level arbiter in CI.
- The PR's CI is the real gate; no fake test output.

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

The failing check is `kicker / sm-liveness` from the sm-kicker workflow — which is a watchdog/kicker job, not a test of the PR code. The known upstream defect awf#15 mentions crashes on zero-diff merge heads. The sm-liveness job is part of the factory watchdog. Without ci_failures_full.log, I can't see the exact error. Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the

    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI

The CI failure is `gh: Server Error (HTTP 502)` from a `gh api` call in the sm-liveness kicker job — a transient GitHub API error, completely unrelated to the PR code. Per the rules: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING". Hmm, but the machine protocol says CI failures = BLOCKING. However, this is clearly an infrastructure flake (HTTP 502 from GitHub's API), not a code issue. The instruction formatting_rules F7 says: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)".

But verdict rules say BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI)... "failing gates (red CI)" is listed as BLOCKING. However, this specific failure is a transient 502 from a watchdog kicker job that is not a PR gate (it's a scheduled kicker, not a required check on the PR — required contexts are Quality gate, JS engine integration, Binaries smoke gate). The kicker runs on push to any non-main branch + cron; its failure doesn't block merge.

I should note it honestly: report the CI failure, classify it as an infra flake (transient HTTP 502), not a code defect. Per the mechanical rules, red CI = blocking. But the failure is in a non-gating watchdog job caused by GitHub API 502. The verdict rule anti-patterns warn against REQUEST_CHANGES with blocking=0. I could include it as BLOCKING per F7... but that would trigger another rework round for something unfixable in code — the anti-pattern is about not blocking on suggestion-level nits; a transient infra 502 is also not a code fix.

Hmm. The instructions are binding-ish: F7 says include each failure as BLOCKING. The CI failure is real (the check failed on this commit). But it's clearly a transient GitHub 502 in an external watchdog job. The pragmatic and honest approach: note it in the general comment as an infra flake that will re-run/needs re-kick, and since no code-level blocking findings exist, verdict... 

Let me think about what the "machine" would do. If I mark BLOCKING=1 with REQUEST_CHANGES, a rework round runs, author pushes nothing meaningful, 15-20 CI minutes wasted. The failure is `gh: Server Error (HTTP 502)` — transient. The verdict rules say "failing gates (red CI)" = BLOCKING. But is kicker/sm-liveness a gate? Required contexts are the three named. Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

messages.preview: CI failure root cause found: transient `gh: Server Error (HTTP 502)` in the kicker watchdog job — not a code defect. Now the deep code review.

blocks.text:
The CI failure is `gh: Server Error (HTTP 502)` from a `gh api` call in the sm-liveness kicker job — a transient GitHub API error, completely unrelated to the PR code. Per the rules: "If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING". Hmm, but the machine protocol says CI failures = BLOCKING. However, this is clearly an infrastructure flake (HTTP 502 from GitHub's API), not a code issue. - **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-12T12:28:15Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1554

Every surface that pins a model endpoint — `roles:` chain entries and `customProviders:` entries (plus the gh-1398 `models.custom` surface) — can carry `connectTimeoutMs`/`streamIdleTimeoutMs`; per FIELD the first level that declares a value wins:

```
role chain entry > customProviders entry > models.custom entry
    > global providerTimeouts: > built-in default (connect 180s, idle 300s)
```

## Delivered (AC checklist)

- [x] **AC1** — roles chain entry timeouts ride the built `Model` (`connectTimeout`/`streamIdleTimeout` + `timeoutScopeLabel` = `role <role> override`) — request-scoped, so they drive the watchdogs for THAT role's streams only, work for catalog-default baseUrls (never URL-seedable before), and two entries on one endpoint keep separate windows. UT: resolver builds labeled models per role, per-field absence stays null. IT (loopback): scoped 1s window fires for its model while a second model in the same session takes the 3s global window; stall line names `idle window 1s (role slow override)`, the unscoped model's does not.
- [x] **AC2** — `customProviders:` entry timeouts scope every resolution through the entry: main provider + roles refs naming its kind+baseUrl resolve through the URL-keyed table (boot seeding, both CLI and app — `bin/fah.dart` IS the CLI boot, `fah_runapp.dart` is its part file).
- [x] **AC3** — the full precedence table per field: `ProviderTuningRegistry.matchesForUrl` returns matching entries in priority order (depth desc, later registration first); `resolveProviderTimeouts` + both wire helpers walk the chain per field, so an entry overriding only the idle leg falls through to the lower surface's connect leg instead of jumping to global. Seed order fixed to `models.custom < customProviders < roleRefs < queue` (the old order inverted customProviders vs models.custom). UTs: mixed-field fall-through, same-field collision, global/default reach, wire-helper agreement, seed-order table.
- [x] **AC4** — backward compat: all new fields nullable; every untouched config resolves byte-identically (empty registry fast paths intact; stall messages unchanged when no scope is in effect; gh-1398 parser suites untouched and still pin valid/absent/malformed/0/negative/over-1h on all four surfaces). The connect stall trace now reports the EFFECTIVE budget (was the raw global default even when a table entry resolved lower — latent gh-1398 inconsistency, fixed in passing).
- [x] **AC5** — docs: new "Scoped provider timeouts" section in `docs/agents/providers.md` (precedence table + slow-local-model recipe) and the `self-settings` skill (`prompts/skills/self-settings/SKILL.md` keys + paragraph; `prompts.g.dart` synced — see gate note).

Design pt 4: stall error lines and `[net]` replay lines keep their shape; a scoped override appends the naming fragment (`— idle window 1800s (role smol override)` / `(<source>)` before the pinned watchdog tags — contains-matching classifiers unaffected).

## Remaining

# SM kicker — thin stub over the canonical watchdog in the factory home.
# All logic (sm-liveness + head-completeness) lives in
# IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml;
# defaults below match this repo (ci.yml, three required contexts).
name: SM kicker

run-name: '🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}'

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  # Event-driven wake-up (2026-10-03, parity with dmtools-dart#338):
  # GitHub starved both crons (machine-sm */10 + kicker 13,43) for 100
  # minutes on dmtools-dart; a green validation verdict sat unlatched the
  # whole window. CI conclusions are the verdict moments — react to them
  # and latching/FIFO-arming happen within seconds, cron or no cron.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

jobs:
  kicker:
    # Tracks dmtools-agentic-workflows @main — always-latest policy (owner
    # directive 2026-10-04): kicker fixes (real ticks awf#13, per-head-SHA
    # concurrency awf#14) go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony; the
    # concurrency scoping lives in the reusable workflow. Guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    #
    # KNOWN UPSTREAM DEFECT (awf#15, live on awf@main as of 2026-10-04):
    # the head-completeness job's `gh api` calls put `--jq` BEFORE
    # `--arg`/`--argjson`, so gh eats the flag as the --jq value and the
    # rest become positional args — `accepts 1 arg(s), received 4`, exit 1.
    # Trigger shape: a CODELESS branch head (2 parents, 0 changed files —
    # a routine branch-sync merge with no content diff). Code-bearing
    # heads skip before the broken lines, so only zero-diff merge heads
    # crash the job — and they crash it even when CI is fully green (the
    # crash precedes the required-contexts check), so the job's own
    # rescue dispatch can never heal the exact heads it exists for.
    # Resolution until the upstream fix lands: keep the branch head
    # CODE-BEARING — the next real commit re-enables the healthy
    # code-bearing-head skip. Diagnosed 2026-10-04 on run 37193754301
    # (head 1fe9b1232, a zero-diff sync merge).
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-sm-kicker.yml@main
    with:
      sm_workflow: machine-sm.yml
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
      ci_display_name: CI
      required_contexts: 'Quality gate,JS engine integration (quickjs-ng),Binaries smoke gate'

But verdict rules say BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI)... "failing gates (red CI)" is listed as BLOCKING. However, this specific failure is a transient 502 from a watchdog kicker job that is not a PR gate (it's a scheduled kicker, not a required check on the PR — required contexts are Quality gate, JS engine integration, Binaries smoke gate). The kicker runs on push to any non-main branch + cron; its failure doesn't block merge.

I should note it honestly: report the CI failure, classify it as an infra flake (transient HTTP 502), not a code defect. Per the mechanical rules, red CI = blocking. I could include it as BLOCKING per F7... but that would trigger another rework round for something unfixable in code — the anti-pattern is about not blocking on suggestion-level nits; a transient infra 502 is also not a code fix.

But it's clearly a transient GitHub 502 in an external watchdog job. The pragmatic and honest approach: note it in the general comment as an infra flake that will re-run/needs re-kick, and since no code-level blocking findings exist, verdict...
